comparison.heading: Why Fishki?
comparison.intro: Medical students need a fast editor and a serious review system. Today's tools usually deliver only one of them.

products.name: Traditional apps
products.label: Powerful, but complicated
products.text: Strong review algorithms, but a dated interface, difficult setup and slow creation of richer cards.

products.name: Simple flashcard apps
products.label: Simple, but limited
products.text: Pleasant and fast card creation, but too little control for demanding medical exam preparation.

products.name: Fishki
products.label: Simple creation. Advanced reviews.
products.text: A fast editor, flexible study modes and tools for images, tables and long medical answers.

stories.completed: Done. You reached the final study summary screen.

items.title: New deck → 2 cards
items.description: Create a deck, add two basic cards and study them through to the summary.
steps: Tap “Add deck” and create a new set.
Add the first basic card and tap “Next”.
Add the second card and tap “Save” to return to the deck.
Tap “Study” in the top-right corner of the deck.
Go through the cards until the summary screen.

items.title: New deck → cloze
items.description: Create a deck, add one cloze card and finish a short study session.
steps: Tap “Add deck” and create a new set.
Select part of the text, use cloze and tap “Save”.
Tap “Study” in the top-right corner of the deck.
Go through study until the summary screen.

items.title: Ready deck → study
items.description: Start studying from an example deck and reach the repeat-or-exit choice.
steps: Tap “Study” on one of the example decks.
Rate each card as “I know” or “I don't know”.
On the final screen, choose repeat or return to the deck.

research.heading: Built from conversations with medical students
research.description: The same problems kept coming up: creating flashcards takes too long, images are poorly supported, reviews become chaotic and offline access is not good enough. Fishki focuses on exactly those problems.
insights: Fast flashcard creation matters, but not at the expense of advanced editing features.
Images are essential for anatomy, histology and diagrams.
Offline access is a real need, not a nice extra.

proof.heading: What medical students want from a flashcard tool
proof.description: These comments show which problems Fishki is designed to tackle first: faster creation, better image workflows, study modes, exam planning and reliable offline access.

quotes.name: Łukasz
quotes.quote: I would like to mark the exact points in an answer that I do not remember, so that during the next review the app hides those specific fragments. An exam mode and automatic increase in reviews before the deadline would also be very useful.

quotes.name: Hania
quotes.quote: The most important thing would be easy access to flashcards from other users, but also a review algorithm like in Anki. I would like to make flashcards on a tablet, continue on my phone and have everything available offline with sync when the internet comes back.

quotes.name: Kasia
quotes.quote: What would help me most is a combination of Anki and Quizlet: sometimes a quick review split into I know / I do not know, and sometimes normal spaced repetition. A hint before showing the answer would also be nice, for example a mnemonic or association.

quotes.name: Marta
quotes.quote: I often study in places without internet, for example on a train, and in Quizlet downloading decks can get stuck. For me, a big plus would be offline access that simply works and gives confidence that the flashcards are really downloaded.

quotes.name: Ola
quotes.quote: Quizlet has nice study modes, for example typing the answer manually or ABCD tests, but I miss more control over reviews. I would like to manually change intervals, shuffle flashcards or study them in order, and easily swap question-answer sides.
